statements.text: AI is going to be a component—and has to be a component—of our strategy in our military going forward. We are not having the level of conversations, though, on some of the risks that we need to have, right? The use of AI and targeting being a good example…I'm somebody that believes that there always must be a human involved in the kill chain, and that we should not be making decisions to take lives based on an AI algorithm. We need to be able to make those decisions as humans, and those are discussions that we're going to have to have.

statements.text: When several companies, not just one, but several companies and civilian leaders and AI experts come to us and say, ‘Hey, there's a 10% chance that it will destroy humanity in the next couple of years.’ We should listen to that.

But we need to pump the brakes. We need to slow things down to buy time so that we can put regulations and guardrails in place for the safe and responsible use of AI that doesn’t have catastrophic consequences.

Congress has a responsibility to act on AI.

Instead of voting and debating on proper guardrails, Speaker Johnson sent us home early.

AI should benefit all of society—not just enrich big corporations or the elite.

We should go back into session to take action. https://t.co/rDqUxNNwth
